textRegions.tex: \textbf{5}\quad\text{The graph of }y=x^3+bx^2+cx+d\text{ is shown opposite, where }b,c,d\text{ are real constants.}\quad\begin{array}{ll}\textbf{a}&\text{Find the values of }b,c,d.\quad\text{(3 marks)}\\\textbf{b}&\text{Write down the coordinates of the point where the curve crosses the }y\text{-axis. (1 mark)}\end{array}

transcription.tex: \begin{aligned}\textbf{a}\quad y&=x^3+bx^2+cx+d\\y&=(x+3)(x+2)(x-1)\\&=(x+3)(x^2+x-2)\\&=x^3+4x^2+x-6\\&b=4,\ c=1,\ d=-6\end{aligned}
transcription.notes: Visually checked original raster; visible labels and working retained.

transcription.tex: \textbf{b}\quad\text{When }x=0,\ y=-6.\text{ So the curve crosses the }y\text{-axis at }(0,-6).
transcription.notes: Visually checked original raster; visible labels and working retained.

textRegions.tex: \textbf{6}\quad\text{The graph of }y=ax^3+bx^2+cx+d\text{ is shown opposite, where }a,b,c,d\text{ are real constants. Find the values of }a,b,c,d.\quad\text{(4 marks)}

transcription.tex: \begin{aligned}y&=ax^3+bx^2+cx+d\\y&=a(x+1)(x-2)(x-3)\\&=a(x+1)(x^2-5x+6)\\&=a(x^3-4x^2+x+6)\\&\text{The curve crosses the }y\text{-axis at }(0,2),\text{ so when }x=0,\ y=2.\\2&=a(0-0+0+6)\\a&=\tfrac13\\y&=\tfrac13(x^3-4x^2+x+6)\\&=\tfrac13x^3-\tfrac43x^2+\tfrac13x+2\\&a=\tfrac13,\ b=-\tfrac43,\ c=\tfrac13,\ d=2\end{aligned}
transcription.notes: Visually checked original raster; visible labels and working retained.

transcription.notes: Visually checked original raster; visible labels and working retained.

transcription.tex: \begin{aligned}y&=(x+5)(x-4)(x^2+5x+14)\\&\text{The discriminant of the quadratic factor}\\&=b^2-4ac\\&=5^2-4\times1\times14\\&=-31,\text{ so there are no real roots.}\\0&=(x+5)(x-4)(x^2+5x+14)\\&x=-5,\ x=4\text{ or }x^2+5x+14=0\\&\text{The curve crosses the }x\text{-axis at }(-5,0)\text{ and }(4,0).\\&\text{When }x=0,\ y=5\times(-4)\times14=-280\\&\text{So the curve crosses the }y\text{-axis at }(0,-280).\\&x\to\infty,\ y\to\infty\\&x\to-\infty,\ y\to\infty\end{aligned}

(3 marks)}\end{array}

transcription.tex: \begin{aligned}\textbf{d}\quad&(x+1)(x+2)(3x-2)=0\\&\text{So }x=-1,\ x=-2\text{ or }x=\tfrac23\\&\text{Using }y=3x+7:\\&\text{when }x=-1,\ y=3(-1)+7=4\\&\text{when }x=-2,\ y=3(-2)+7=1\\&\text{when }x=\tfrac23,\ y=3(\tfrac23)+7=9\\&\text{So the points of intersection are }(-1,4),(-2,1)\text{ and }(\tfrac23,9).\end{aligned}

transcription.tex: \begin{aligned}\textbf{b}\quad&\text{From the sketch, there are no points of intersection of the curves. This means there are no values of }x\text{ where}\\&x^2+1=\tfrac12x-\tfrac12\\&2x^2+2=x-1\\&2x^2-x+3=0\\&\text{So this equation has no real solutions.}\end{aligned}
transcription.notes: Visually checked original raster; exact text and working retained; original graph retained where mixed.

transcription.tex: \begin{aligned}\textbf{c}\quad x^2+a&=\tfrac12x-\tfrac12\\2x^2+2a&=x-1\\2x^2-x+2a+1&=0\\&\text{Using the discriminant for two real roots,}\\b^2-4ac&>0\\(-1)^2-4(2)(2a+1)&>0\\1-16a-8&>0\\-16a-7&>0\\16a&<-7\\a&<-\tfrac7{16}\end{aligned}

transcription.tex: \begin{aligned}\textbf{b}\quad&\text{From the sketch, there are two points of intersection of the curves. This means there are two values of }x\text{ where}\\&x^2(x-1)(x+1)=\tfrac13x^3+1\\&3x^2(x-1)(x+1)=x^3+3\\&\text{So this equation has two real solutions.}\end{aligned}
